papers.title: Probabilistic Programming with Gaussian Process Memoization
papers.abstract: Gaussian Processes (GPs) are widely used tools in statistics, machine learning, robotics, computer vision, and scientific computation. However, despite their popularity, they can be difficult to apply; all but the simplest classification or regression applications require specification and inference over complex covariance functions that do not admit simple analytical posteriors. This paper shows how to embed Gaussian processes in any higher-order probabilistic programming language, using an idiom based on memoization, and demonstrates its utility by implementing and extending classic and state-of-the-art GP applications. The interface to Gaussian processes, called gpmem, takes an arbitrary real-valued computational process as input and returns a statistical emulator that automatically improve as the original process is invoked and its input-output behavior is recorded. The flexibility of gpmem is illustrated via three applications: (i) robust GP regression with hierarchical hyper-parameter learning, (ii) discovering symbolic expressions from time-series data by fully Bayesian structure learning over kernels generated by a stochastic grammar, and (iii) a bandit formulation of Bayesian optimization with automatic inference and action selection. All applications share a single 50-line Python library and require fewer than 20 lines of probabilistic code each.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该方法提出了通过记忆化将高斯过程嵌入概率编程的通用框架，但未涉及有限元替代建模、约束处理或生物力学应用，仅为背景性方法参考。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address FEA surrogate modeling, constraint handling, or implant/biomechanics design; it focuses on probabilistic programming infrastructure for GP emulation without any physical simulation validation.

summary_en.motivation: To simplify the specification and inference of Gaussian processes within probabilistic programming languages.
summary_en.method: Embed Gaussian processes into a universal probabilistic programming language via a memoization idiom, returning a statistical emulator that improves as the process is invoked.
summary_en.result: Demonstrated flexibility on three applications: robust GP regression, symbolic expression discovery, and Bayesian optimization with automatic inference.
summary_en.validation: No physical simulation validation; only tested on standard machine learning and synthetic benchmarks.

papers.title: Energy component in the density of selective laser melting fabricated prototype
papers.first_author_affiliation: School of Civil and Environmental Engineering, Nanyang Technological University, 50 Nanyang Avenue, Singapore, 639798, Singapore

corresponding_authors.name: M. M. Savalani
corresponding_authors.affiliation: Department of Industrial and Systems Engineering, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Kowloon, Hong Kong

papers.venue: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文聚焦于SLM工艺参数与致密度关系，未涉及生物医学植入物的应力屏蔽、疲劳或骨整合等方向。
llm.why_not_core: Does not address porous structures, stress shielding, fatigue, surface roughness, or osseointegration in biomedical implants; purely a process-parameter study for density optimization.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究能量密度对选区激光熔化原型致密度的影响机制
summary_zh.method: 通过改变激光功率和扫描速度制备不同能量密度的SLM试样
summary_zh.result: 建立了能量密度与致密度之间的定量关系
summary_zh.validation: 采用密度测量验证工艺参数与致密度的相关性

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the effect of energy density on the density of selective laser melting (SLM) fabricated prototypes.
summary_en.method: SLM specimens were fabricated with varying laser power and scanning speed to achieve different energy density levels.
summary_en.result: A quantitative relationship between energy density and part density was established.
summary_en.validation: Density measurements were used to validate the correlation between process parameters and part density.
